transcript: For years now, we've talked quite a bit about the somewhat depressingly low level of tech literacy among policymakers just on this podcast in the past few months. We've talked to Betsy Cooper about teaching technologists how to engage on policy as well. And we've talked to Daniel Schulman and Zach Graves about how to better inform Congress about technology issues. So we're always excited when it appears that any policy maker takes a serious interest in Any of these things that we're interested in at Tech Dirt and one who has definitely done a lot on this front recently is Representative Mark Zakano from California's 41st Congressional District. He's recently introduced two pieces of legislation, both of which I think are of great interest to the tech dirt community. The first is the Office of Technology Assessment Improvement and Enhancement Act. As we've discussed, the OTA was an independent non-partisan agency that used to inform Congress about technology issues until it was completely defunded in 1995. For over a decade now, we've talked about the importance of bringing back the OTA, and there's finally some appearance that that may be happening with the latest appropriations bill and with this new act. Congressman Takano is looking to make the OTA even better. The second recent bill that he's introduced is the Justice and Forensic Algorithms Act, which touches on another issue we've covered a picture quite a lot as our courts and law enforcement systems have grown ever more dependent on technology, defendants in court cases often don't actually have access to the underlying technology that could have a major impact on their lives. We've told many stories of defendants who wanted to understand the algorithms that are effectively deciding their fate, only to be told that it's a trade secret or otherwise proprietary. This bill would require such source code to be available. Now, both of these are obviously very interesting and important proposals, and here to talk about them is Congressman Takano. Thanks for joining us.
